data.title: KSrelief's Masam Project Clears 1,269 Landmines, Unexploded Ordnance in Yemen in One Week
data.content:
Aden, November 22, 2026, SPA -- The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center's (KSrelief) Masam Project for Landmine Clearance in Yemen removed 1,269 explosive devices across various regions of Yemen during the third week of November, including eight anti-personnel mines, 89 anti-tank mines, and 1,172 unexploded ordnance items.
    The total number of mines and unexploded ordnance cleared since the beginning of November has reached 3,599, bringing the overall number removed since the launch of the Masam Project to 603,599. These devices were planted indiscriminately across Yemen by the Houthi terrorist militia, endangering the lives of innocent civilians, including children, women, and the elderly, and spreading fear among communities.
    Saudi Arabia, through its humanitarian arm KSrelief, continues its efforts to clear Yemeni territory of landmines under a project aimed at enhancing civilian safety and enabling the Yemeni people to live in dignity and security.
    
    -- SPA
